takeaway: Chief (peptic) cells secrete pepsinogen. Parietal cells make acid and intrinsic factor, G-cells gastrin, goblet cells mucus, D-cells somatostatin, ECL cells histamine.

question.text: Which cells in the gastric wall secrete pepsinogen?

lines.text: Look at the stomach wall: it is deeply folded.
The folds form gastric glands, which open into the lumen at the gastric pits.
Inside the glands sit different secretory cells, each with its own product.
Our chef, the chief or peptic cell, pours out pepsinogen.
Parietal cells make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.
G-cells make gastrin. D-cells make somatostatin, and ECL cells make histamine.
So pepsinogen comes from the chief cells.
